# Represent next-open fixtures in the native CLI

## Problem and evidence

The v0.30.0 report CLI at producer commit
`4ab0fde8dfcfd3f2b33e4ea0af6186474c2b6ffa` fixes close fills,
zero fees and starting equity 10000. In `report/run.go` (Git blob
`0441c704251e2178e4a2c3d0b7afacaef2590f1c`), both preparation and
execution use close fills. The original shared fixtures
`family-named-level-flag` and `family-named-level-flag-short-only`
require nextOpen. Their complete released Go/WASM and shared JS goldens
match, while the report CLI executes a different fill contract.

On 2026-10-11 the owner approved the bounded consumer coverage correction:
58 native report cases / 348 stat comparisons; all 109 complete original
WASM fixture results; all 60 shared JS cases; and 49 actual JS refusal cases.
The two shared nextOpen cases have an explicit native-CLI-unrepresentable
disposition, not a pass or native refusal. This task closes that remaining
native CLI input gap; it does not replace broader native engine qualification.

Exact original identities:

- `family-named-level-flag`: source SHA256
  `54568351e14aa0d5f89a81e4494df9aae69d9b720cc3afe6c8921111000de891`;
  fixture `77365d6354bb3e7671610e998d4a9c0aa22a1387319616f48e15c8d76ce00096`;
  golden `c42fce080f39828735af20d58b13ae807b1e614b2c393b5b7c11eed0ac139c5c`.
- `family-named-level-flag-short-only`: source SHA256
  `6f3b41e12840bc9fdef4193ed1fb55ec9ba3de37af2f409839282e34a572fbc3`;
  fixture `5363e0c34e0e54fa3b2b83bb78688cf84a9587dbaf5042501daa79475f6bbb8f`;
  golden `d45cdff02adc818e505c58cc88d17c3a23ee28ac168853092eb9b47133888260`.

## Bounded implementation decision before claiming source paths

The smallest report-specific repair is an explicit validated fill-mode input,
threaded through preparation and execution, preserving the current default
close behavior and all old CLI outputs. Review the exact route and option
semantics before edits; do not silently reinterpret existing flags.

Also assess whether a native fixture subcommand reusing the existing
run-fixture-v1 / engineRunFixture dispatch is the better durable boundary.
It could carry complete original fixtures and compare native/WASM envelopes
without a second strategy implementation. That is an alternative reviewed
scope, not approval to expand this task automatically.

## Acceptance

- Preserve original source, fixture and golden bytes. Both nextOpen cases must
  execute with their original fill contract; a close-only control is diagnostic.
- Keep close as the existing report default, validate invalid/unknown modes,
  and exercise mixed/repeated invocations with no leaked configuration.
- Use one Go engine. No new JS strategy, duplicated execution logic, regenerated
  golden, numerical tolerance change or historical market outcome is authorized.
- Requalify exact source/compiler schedules on required native architectures
  and WASM. A source inventory amendment must be independently reviewed.
- Independently review the final scoped source and all existing CLI regressions.
  Release through the normal verified policy only after exact-head checks pass;
  choose the version from actual release policy, not this planning record.
- Consumer adoption must verify genuine published asset digests and remove
  exceptions only after the original fixtures pass the new native interface.
  Continue reporting actual per-interface coverage honestly.

Fees, configurable starting equity, initial positions, pending orders,
checkpoint/restart, paper-forward, calendar policy and historical outcomes are
not implicitly included. The current fixture schema carries no initial-position
or checkpoint contract. If broader fixture transport is chosen, record its
precise supported fields and refusal behavior in a fresh bounded claim.

## Creation and ownership

### Prospective producer claim, 2026-10-22

Codex claims only the report CLI fill input on current Strat main
`500a31e1d280eda5126f7c12c3f79b1164d176bb`. Exact maintained paths:
`report/run.go`, `report/build.go`, `cmd/heisentick/report.go`,
`cmd/heisentick/main.go`, `report/run_test.go`, `report/build_test.go`, and
`cmd/heisentick/main_test.go`. Validate `close|nextOpen`, retain close as the
default and grid behavior, thread the selected mode through preparation and
execution, and test both original nextOpen cases without changing their bytes.
Acceptance also checks invalid modes, repeated/mixed invocation isolation,
old CLI golden bytes, `gofmt -l .`, `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...`,
`go run ./cmd/conformance check`, and `git diff --check`. This claim excludes
engine, broker, parser, conformance corpus/goldens, applications, workflows,
release and consumer pins. Draft source publication is recorded below; source
merge and release remain held for root review. Independent design review found a native fixture subcommand
would require a broader transport contract and is outside this slice.

### Prospective qualification pin repair, 2026-10-22

The seven-path source claim above and its history remain intact. After draft
Strat PR 149 passed Go tests and goldens, ordinary stamped native/public-WASM
qualification stopped at the source admission gate: the reviewed report CLI
source changed while the existing arithmetic inventory still names the prior
source bytes. This amendment adds exactly
`scripts/checks/sequential-arithmetic-schedules.json` to the producer write set
for a reviewed inventory-only renewal. Only four changed production-source
SHA-256 values and the matching `report/build.go` and `report/run.go` hashes in
each of the three existing target `buildInputs.files` records may change.
Instruction schedule pins must remain byte-for-byte unchanged, as must target
keys, package closure, accounting schedules, compiler/build settings,
`sourceParents`, proof scripts and ordinary `EXTRA_PINS`. Compare the manifest
before and after by path and field, independently recompute each source hash,
and review exact compiler streams on supported Linux hosts before treating
qualification as passed. The local Mac preparation is not Linux execution or
all-target qualification. No release, consumer pin or deployment is included.

### Prospective sampled bid/ask diagnostic, 2026-10-22

Draft Strat PR 149 then passed ordinary stamped native/public-WASM qualification
at the inventory-renewed head but its sampled bid/ask parity step reached the
existing 20-minute CI limit after the Go WASM bridge test passed. The parity
harness prints only a final summary, so the stalled case is unknown. Prior main
runs of this unchanged workload took roughly 16–19 minutes. This diagnostic
claim adds exactly `scripts/checks/paper-bidask-parity.mjs` to the HT-257 write
set for bounded progress messages naming synthetic case/phase, native or WASM,
and elapsed time. No raw inputs or credentials may be logged. Input ordering,
assertions, financial/runtime code, limits, timeouts, runners and workflow
settings remain unchanged. Validate with a cheap synthetic/mock path or static
comparison; do not run the full workload on the shared Mac. Publish a source
candidate only after independent review. Normal PR CI may then provide case
timing evidence; manual reruns and AMD64 qualification are separate holds.
